catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class controls a simulator's wall-time lapse lock. cap.motion.stop.v1 is a motion stop for the robot.arm, robot.mobile_base and motion.axis kinds and is not simulation control; cap.world.step.v1 advances a world and does not pause it. The extension reports the upstream nb_holders count and is also the e-stop binding.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). No ROS graph, Gazebo world, ArduPilot SITL process, simulator run or hardware run was performed or is claimed. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null; no hardware backend is declared, and RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review.

SHAPE AND SCOPE: the pinned upstream is a ROS 1/Gazebo WorldPlugin library, not a standalone ROS node. This is a configuration-only RosDriver over rosbridge with no Python native class and no native.py. The operator loads the plugin in a Gazebo world and runs ArduPilot SITL and rosbridge separately. The served surface is the one the clone declares: the acknowledged /fdmUDP/take_apm_lapseLock and /fdmUDP/release_apm_lapseLock services (ardupilot_sitl_gazebo_plugin/src/apm_plugin_ros_side.cpp:77-78, NodeHandle namespace /fdmUDP at apm_plugin_ros_side.cpp:45 and header:93; service types at header:72-73), and a fresh subscription to /cessna/command/motor_speed with mav_msgs/CommandMotorSpeed (publisher at apm_plugin_ros_side.cpp:73-74; include at header:52; the LFLY Cessna world sets UAV_MODEL=cessna at worlds/LFLY_world_cessna/empty.world:88; the Cessna aircraft plugin uses the same resolved topic at urdf/aircraft_base.xacro:419). The Cessna topic is a deployment assumption, not a remapping: a deployment that selects another model name must expose that model's /<modelName>/command/motor_speed or the read fails. There is no default rosbridge destination; the hardware endpoint stays operator-supplied.

SAFETY: mode simulated, device_kind world.sim, risk R0. The only native pause is the wall-time lapse lock. The ordinary take action uses the upstream take_lapseLock method default of 1 s (header:113, header:146) because the service requires the caller's max_duration. The e-stop binding is the same take service with a fixed max_duration equal to the maximum finite value of the declared float32 field (srv/TakeApmLapseLock.srv:2), so the upstream wall-time timer does not expire in a realistic deployment. This is a request choice, not a Limit or a device safety bound. The e-stop stops the plugin's stepping loop: while check_lapseLock returns false the loop skips receive_apm_input, Gazebo Step and FDM output (ardupilot_sitl_gazebo_plugin.cpp:241-244, 326-345). It does not stop the ArduPilot SITL process, and it is not an independent stop: the upstream header states the lock has no memory or identification of holding processes and an external release can resume the simulation before a holder finishes (header:285-310). The MHS software latch refuses this driver's own take/release commands while latched. No physical e-stop, hardware run, torque-off, independent quiescence or safety certification is claimed. The safe_state sentence states this limitation. site-limits.example.json is not needed because no caller input has a numeric bound; the 1 s and maximum-float32 horizons are request values, not operator bounds.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: fake.py is a ROS-free mhs.bridge.ros_transport.RecordingRosTransport, not a recording of captured traffic and not the upstream simulator. It is F0, engine analytic, determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0, reset none, no snapshot/restore. It answers the declared subscription and services, records the service requests, and models application and transport failures. It runs no Gazebo, SITL, UDP socket, physics step or wall-clock loop; every state value is placeholder test data. The fake keeps its placeholder lapse lock held until release or a test reset and does not run the upstream elapsed-wall-time expiry; the real plugin also clears the lock automatically. The plugin's 2.5 ms SITL step and loop rates are source facts, not fake timing.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds nine repository cases: the motor-speed observation, take/release reaching the two upstream services, a failed take service, a take application failure with an external holder, a malformed take response as an unknown outcome, a release application failure with a remaining holder, no fresh motor sample while the lock is held, the e-stop taking the lapse lock and pausing the observation, and the e-stop latch refusing further take commands. Warnings kept from the last gate run: G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected because no caller input declares a numeric limit, so the out-of-limit probe has nothing to test; every other CL3 test passed. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings.

NOT COVERED: the SITL UDP bridge (ports 9002/9003), FDM packets, servo packets, sensor topics and callbacks, the parachute path, Gazebo stepping and physics, rotor dynamics, the aircraft_plugin and liftdrag_plugin consumers, the recorder_camera_plugin and all image artifacts, ROS parameters, QoS, namespace/remapping other than the stated resolved endpoints, live ROS graph behaviour and any hardware. No Limit is declared because the exposed actions have no numeric caller input and the observation states no sourced bound. The clone was left unmodified; no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked endpoints, types, all facts, the fake and the stop at the pin; the e-stop holds as an acknowledged simulator pause, since the plugin keeps Gazebo paused and steps it only from the loop that a held lapse lock skips (apm_plugin_gazebo_side.cpp:66, 101-109; ardupilot_sitl_gazebo_plugin.cpp:241-262), and reset does not release it. Defects: three facts said more than their lines; the observation declared rad/s although the Cessna aircraft plugin reads the entries as control-surface and propeller commands; safe_state omitted that the freeze needs Gazebo to stay paused and that any release to zero clears the lock (an expired holder, the parachute path); a probe showed the take is not idempotent (a repeated e-stop fails the exact nb_holders predicate and the retry keeps adding holders; fail-safe but undisclosed); and only LFLY_world_cessna.launch publishes the bound topic. The reviewer rewrote safe_state, the docstring, the observation schema and the take description, corrected the three facts, added 29 source facts and six gaps, including two upstream defects at the pin and a licence conflict (driver.py), added an e-stop case with another holder (test_driver.py), updated facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:b5fdc9a6862589c743abe22d0b35eec03b214c348857853dd1f41ef55022ccb0); ten package cases pass, so the author's count of nine is stale. For the human reviewer: Simulator only (Gazebo plugin bridged to ArduPilot SITL over localhost UDP). The e-stop freezes the aircraft mid-flight while ArduPilot SITL runs on; the freeze ends if a client unpauses Gazebo (the aircraft plugin then applies the last command) or any release brings the holder count to zero. A repeated e-stop is reported SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held and the SDK retry adds a holder per attempt until reset; resuming needs one release_lapse_lock per take (reset does not resume). Upstream defects at the pin: in the LFLY world NB_SERVOS_MOTOR_SPEED 5 indexes _cmd_motor_speed[4] past its 4-entry array (undefined behaviour); empty_world_cessna's Cessna listens on a topic the plugin does not publish. Licence: the card says Apache-2.0 with publish_review not_required, but SocketAPM.cpp/.h, compiled into the plugin library, are GPL-3.0-or-later copies from ArduPilot and the plugin package.xml says TODO; the owner decides publication.
